collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager who uses a walking frame asks for the dance ground to be made level: rebuild it, or move the dances somewhere flatter.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) uses a walking frame made of bamboo, and gets around the village perfectly well, except for the dance ground, which is all roots and slopes and rocks. (subject.He/she) has missed the last three dances. Today (subject.he/she) has asked the village, plainly, to fix it. (friend) is in charge of the dances. What should (friend) do?

choices.label: Move the Dances to the Beach

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (friend) gets everyone digging. It takes four days to level the ground, pull out the roots and pack the earth smooth. At the next dance, (subject) is in the middle of it, and the children discover that a level dance ground is also perfect for rolling things on.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) suggests holding the dances on the flat, hard sand by the water. (subject) agrees to try it. The sand is good for the frame but terrible for the drums, which keep getting wet. The dances move twice more before everyone is happy. Nobody suggests going back to the old ground.
